title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
An elevation map is given as n non-negative integers, each the height of a bar of width 1. After it rains, water collects between the bars. Compute how many units of water are trapped in total.

Input format
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n non-negative integers (the heights, left to right).

Output format
One integer: the total units of trapped water.
hints: Think about a single bar. How high can the water above it get, and what decides that?
The water above bar i is min(tallest bar to its left, tallest bar to its right) - height[i], if that is positive. Computing both maxima for every bar gives an O(n) answer with two helper arrays.
You can save memory with two pointers moving inward: always advance the side whose current maximum is smaller, because that side is limited by its own maximum.

examples.explanation: Water collects in the dips between the taller bars; the total is 6 units.
The bars 4 and 5 hold 9 units between them.
